item.title: Pochettino appointed as Man Utd boss after Carrick sacking
item.description: USA coach Mauricio Pochettino has replaced the sacked Michael Carrick at Manchester United (JAMIE SQUIRE) Mauricio Pochettino was named Manchester United's new manager on Friday, tasked with reviving the struggling giants following the dismissal of Michael Carrick. The Red Devils issued a statement saying the USA coach, who has extensive experience in the Premier League, would take charge from November 18 following two matches against Haiti. The 54-year-old is understood to have signed a two-and-a-half-year deal at Old Trafford, taking him through to the end of the 2028/29 season. "The club has reached an agreement with the US soccer federation for Mauricio and his staff to be released after the conclusion of their responsibilities with the US men's national team," United said. "The Argentinian is renowned for his high-intensity, attacking style of football, his dedication to building strong, cohesive teams and his outstanding record of developing individual players. "Pochettino has consistently performed at the highest level of football across multiple leagues." Pochettino, who led the United States to the last-16 of the World Cup on home soil earlier this year, said in a statement released by US Soccer that the job with the national team had been "one of the greatest honours of my career". "We are so grateful to the players for their commitment, to the fans for their belief, and to the federation for always supporting our staff and creating the opportunities to impact the culture of soccer in this great country," he added. US Soccer CEO and secretary general JT Batson said Pochettino had left a lasting mark on football in the United States through his "leadership, professionalism and commitment to our players and culture". The federation is reportedly set to receive $10 million in compensation for him, plus a further $2 million for the departure of his coaching staff. Pochettino has previously managed Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea in England, and also coached Paris Saint-Germain. He never finished lower than fifth in the Premier League during his five seasons at Tottenham. But despite his relative success at Spurs, Pochettino failed to win silverware and was dismissed in November 2019 -- just months after the north London club lost to Liverpool in the Champions League final. He claimed the first trophies of his managerial career with PSG, collecting the 2021 French Cup and 2022 Ligue 1 title, but did not see out his contract. Pochettino returned to the dugout at Chelsea in 2023 but lasted a single season, reaching the FA Cup semi-finals and losing in the League Cup final. - United slide - Pochettino, who has been linked with the United job on several previous occasions, has a huge task to revive the 20-time English champions, who have endured their worst-ever start to a Premier League campaign. item.title: Celtics’ Winning DNA Showed Up During 4-0 Road Trip
item.description: The NBA Finals aren’t until June, but it’s never too early for a team to hold itself to championship standards. The Celtics showed that on their four-game road trip over the past week. They made that clear with a 22-point comeback against the Toronto Raptors on Wednesday. The night before, they played an emotionally charged game against Jaylen Brown and the 76ers. They had plenty of reasons to slip in Toronto. “We had every excuse in the world,” Derrick White said . Boston was on the second night of a back-to-back, its third game in four days, with Paul George out. But letting up easily isn’t something the Celtics are programmed to do. White and his teammates know the standards in Boston: “The DNA [is] when we put that Celtics uniform on, go out there and win.” A Finals Feel in Philadelphia 76ers fans yelled “sucks” after every Celtic introduced. Loud atmosphere in here. pic.twitter.com/Vgp0h7CgMu — Justin Turpin (@JustinmTurpin) November 11, 2026 Tuesday’s opener of the back-to-back was no typical regular season game. The matchup was a national spectacle. In late October, Brown suggested Jayson Tatum knew more about his trade than he let on. Tatum said there was no “beef or ill will,” to which Brown replied, “there’s no beef, but it might be a little lamb chops and gravy.” Beyond the player drama, the game also featured the two teams with the best records in the Eastern Conference. “I walked out, I couldn’t tell if it was November 10th or June 10th,” Tatum said after the game. “It felt like a f—ing Finals game.” The Celtics built an early double-digit point lead, but saw that erased late in the third quarter. Ghosts of a 22-point second-half collapse against the Detroit Pistons on opening night crept into Celtics fans’ minds, but the team exorcised those demons. The efforts from three members of their 2024 championship team, Tatum, Payton Pritchard, and Sam Hauser, fueled a 12-3 run to close the quarter strong. From there, the forgotten man in the Brown trade, Paul George, took over. He scored 14 of his game-high 36 points in the fourth quarter as the Celtics’ offense exploded and they left the 76ers in the dust. “I remember when Brad Stevens said a couple of years ago that they all count as one,” Tatum said in response to a question about how he stays above the noise surrounding the game. “Tomorrow’s game counts the same as today’s game.” That statement win to claim the best record in the East was a great moment, but it’s hard to come down from a night like that quickly. The Celtics had less than 24 hours to do so. item.description: Man City handed triple boost ahead of Chelsea WSL clash Manchester City Women boss Andree Jegelertz has revealed that Niamh Charles, Beth Mead and Vivianne Miedema are all nearing a return. City are currently top of the WSL two points ahead of Chelsea , with both sides remaining unbeaten. The two teams will meet at Stamford Bridge this Sunday for a huge top-of-the-table clash. Jeglertz will want to be at full strength for the encounter, and could be boosted by a number of injury returnees. “All three of them were in the session today,” the City boss answered on Charles, Mead and Miedema. “And I hope they will be available for Saturday. “It looks good today. We had a day off yesterday and today everybody is back.A good session, full of energy. I feel we are in a good place.” There were also doubts on the availability of Rebecca Knaak, following a head collision in midweek. However, she will also be ready for the trip to Chelsea. Jeglertz confirmed: “She was back in full training. No concern about that.” A rotated City side defeated Inter Milan 4-1 in the Champions League in the week. Jeglertz continued: “We talk about resting players but we also talk about other players getting the opportunity to show they want to compete. “And how important the depth is in the squad and the ones that played on Tuesday were just showing that we have an amazing squad. “Good players no matter who I start I can definitely have players coming in and changing the game. item.title: Michael Carrick sends emotional farewell message to Manchester United fans after dismissal
item.description: Michael Carrick sends emotional farewell message to Manchester United fans after dismissal Michael Carrick has wrote a letter to the Manchester United fans following his departure as head coach. Carrick was dismissed from his role as Manchester United head coach on Thursday, amid the club's worst-ever start to a Premier League campaign. The 45-year-old leaves just five months on from signing a permanent deal, after his interim spell last season. Carrick departs with Manchester United 18th in the Premier League table, having won one of their opening 10 games. Mauricio Pochettino has been named as his replacement. Carrick expressed his gratitude at the chance to lead his former club as manager, thanking the fans for their support. He said the 'love' for Manchester United 'never dies' and hopes for 'nothing but success' for those at Old Trafford. Carrick thanks Manchester United supporters in heartfelt farewell letter “Dear United fans, I've had the immense privilege of leading Manchester United, the football club that I love," he said on Instagram. "There are very few who get to live that and feel it, and for that I'm incredibly grateful.With that comes huge responsibility, and to be at Manchester United, you need to understand exactly what that means. "It's different to anywhere else. "Ultimately, you need to push to be the best, but there is a culture, there are values and there are behaviours that you have to live by and respect, which have been built over a long period of time. It's a football club that is unique, with substance and history that cannot be ignored. This is what inspired me every single day. "I want to say a big thank you to the supporters. I must say, you are a special, rare breed. We've had some great times this year and moments we'll all remember. The best thing about being in my position was seeing so many of you lose yourselves in the emotion of those moments, leaving the stadium desperate to come back again next time. I just wanted to give you something back. "That love never dies. "I know we've not had the results lately, but you've shown me nothing but love and support in times when the easiest thing, and what most end up doing, would be to turn the other way. That means more than a win or two. That's what makes you who you are. That's why I fell in love with this club all those years ago. "A special thank you to my coaching staff. You gave me everything you had, every single day, and I couldn't have asked for any more. I'm incredibly grateful for your loyalty, hard work and support throughout. item.title: Oregon has 3 quarterbacks who could start Saturday. Illinois has a freshman who's never started before
item.description: The Oregon Ducks will face a team on Saturday with an even less desirable quarterback situation. Illinois (3-3, 1-2 Big Ten) quarterback Katin Houser suffered a broken hand that will sideline him for four to six weeks during a 38-37 overtime win over Michigan State on Oct. 10. Oregon has played its last two games without starting quarterback Dante Moore, who suffered a concussion in the second quarter of the Ducks’ 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. However, while Oregon can turn to junior Dylan Raiola — a Nebraska transfer with 23 career starts — and senior Brock Thomas, Illinois is relying on freshman quarterback Michael Clayton II, who will make his first start against the Ducks. A positive for Illinois is that Houser was injured before the team’s bye week, giving coach Bret Bielema two weeks to prepare Clayton. “It was just good timing,” Bielema told reporters during his Monday media session. Illinois is off to a disappointing start after going 9-4 in 2025 and 10-3 in 2024. The defense is below average, while the passing combination of Houser and wide receiver Collin Dixon is one of the nation’s best. Dixon is tied for third nationally with nine touchdown receptions. Illinois head coach Bret Bielema celebrates their overtime win over Michigan State as he walks off the field after an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026, in East Lansing, Mich. (AP Photo/Lon Horwedel) AP Photo/Lon Horwedel AP Photo/Lon Horwedel Now Illinois heads into Saturday’s game against a resurgent Oregon defense, trying to get Clayton up to speed. His performance against MSU elevated expectations. Houser left the game late in the third quarter with Illinois leading 23-10. Clayton completed 6 of 8 passes for 88 yards and two touchdowns. The final touchdown came in overtime on a 25-yard pass that put Illinois up 38-31. Sophomore quarterback Carson Boyd also played. He rushed once for seven yards but did not attempt a pass. Bielema and offensive coordinator Barry Lunney Jr. both said Boyd could play against Oregon (4-2, 2-1), but Clayton is the starter. Usually, Bielema said, his starting quarterback gets a lot of rest during the bye week while the staff works on player development. Given Clayton and Boyd’s inexperience, both got valuable reps in practice last week. “I think those two guys in particular took advantage of every rep,” Bielema said. Bielema has leaned heavily on transfer quarterbacks during his six years at Illinois, including Houser. But that could change if Clayton, a former three-star recruit, earns the job. “I’ve said several times that hopefully the next starter comes from within our program,” Bielema said. Lunney said Clayton will be more prepared than he has in the past given the circumstances. item.title: Reeling Oregon Ducks remain positive, committed to the grind
item.description: EUGENE — The 2026 season is on the verge of completely unraveling for the Oregon Ducks . One more loss, and any shred of postseason hopes would be extinguished. Yet even after two upset losses and falling out of the rankings — despite starting the season at No. 2 — the Ducks (3-2, 1-1 Big Ten) remain focused, together and committed to salvaging the season. “One thing I really love is the way the people in the locker room have been responding to this adversity,” sophomore cornerback Brandon Finney Jr. said. After his team’s 17-15 loss to No. 12 UCLA on Saturday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning said the team would be measured by how it responds moving forward. On Wednesday, he said the team has elevated its work ethic and embraced accountability. “I’ve been proud of the way that they’ve worked,” Lanning said. “I don’t see a lot of hanging heads, right? item.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon’s loss at Illinois and firing of OC Drew Mehringer
item.description: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — The Oregon Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) suffered their worst loss of the season at Illinois on Saturday . The 21-10 defeat came against a marginal Illinois team that started a true freshman at quarterback, rushed for 225 yards, and held Oregon to two scoring drives. As a result, on Sunday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning announced the firing of offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer . What that means for the rest of the season remains to be seen. Mehringer had to contend with several key personnel issues, including starting quarterback Dante Moore missing three games while in concussion protocol. Here are 10 takeaways from Saturday’s game and the firing of Mehringer: 1. It feels like Mehringer is the scapegoat in this mess Criticizing play-calling is an armchair quarterback’s delight, but doing so under Oregon’s current circumstances is somewhat obtuse. Few teams excel without their starting quarterback. The next factor is an offensive line that was clearly mismanaged in the offseason after losing three starters to the NFL. Next is inconsistent play from backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Then sprinkle in losing top wideout Jeremiah McClellan (broken foot) after three games, starting wide receiver Evan Stewart (undisclosed injury) for the last two games, and two more rotational wide receivers heading into Illinois. Does all of that excuse Mehringer for Oregon scoring just 42 points over the past three weeks? No. But those are a lot of obstacles for any offensive coordinator to overcome. Watch " Oregon football fires offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer " on YouTube Watch 2. Where does Lanning go from here? Lanning will probably announce his new offensive coordinator during his Monday press conference. He could promote from within to get through the season and then conduct a national search in the offseason. Or he may have someone in mind to take over now and beyond. Whatever Lanning decides, the next play-caller had better hope Moore returns, or little will change. 3. It could be time to add a veteran coach to the staff Lanning did well by hiring younger offensive coordinators, Kenny Dillingham and then Will Stein. But maybe it’s time to bring in an accomplished, seasoned veteran coach to add a new perspective to a relatively young staff. Someone with a track record of success as an offensive coordinator and maybe as a head coach. Someone like former Oregon coach Chip Kelly, Northwestern’s offensive coordinator. No, don’t expect Kelly to want to return to Oregon. But someone like him could fit perfectly. 4. The wide receiver situation After Saturday’s game, Raiola was asked twice how difficult it was to build timing with the receiving crew, which lacked McClellan, Stewart, and freshmen Messiah Hampton and Jalen Lott. item.title: Dame Time is back in Portland — and the Blazers look dangerous
item.description: A new head coach will roam the sidelines. A franchise icon will make his long-awaited return. An All-Star will begin his redemption tour. And a new ownership group will watch its first season opener from Paul Allen’s former seats along the Moda Center baseline. The Blazers open the 2026-27 NBA season Wednesday night against the Phoenix Suns — a team they upset in April in the play-in tournament — and if you’re just now tuning in for the start of the regular season, well, there’s a lot you missed. RELATED: Suns vs. Blazers predictions, odds and best bets: Dame is home, and the model likes Portland on opening night Let’s catch you up. What does the starting lineup look like? The Blazers are expected to unveil a new starting lineup that features a pair of notable All-Star additions: Damian Lillard and Ja Morant . The backcourt duo is joining a fivesome that includes returning starters Deni Avdija , Toumani Camara and Donovan Clingan . It’s a versatile, star-studded lineup that features three All-Stars, a former All-Defensive Second Team selection, one of the best young centers in the NBA and loads of scoring potential. What about the rotation? Micah Nori , the Blazers’ first-year head coach, said he plans on using a 10-man rotation to start the season, which will allow the Blazers to capitalize on their depth and versatility. In addition to the starters, Jrue Holiday, Scoot Henderson, Sidy Cissoko, Robert Williams III and Vit Krejci are expected to open the season in the rotation. The group could change depending on matchups and Williams’ availability — he did not play in back-to-backs last season — and it’s likely that Micah Potter, Branden Carlson and Yang Hansen will occasionally see spot duty, as well. item.title: OSU's Legree leads nation in receiving as WSU clash looms
item.description: CORVALLIS — There may be no more appropriate way to describe Oregon State’s outrageously successful passing game this season than explosive. The Beavers lead the country in passing yards thanks in large part to 10 passes of 40-plus yards. Jesse Legree is responsible for eight of those catches, including all five of OSU’s 50-yard pass plays this season, making it no surprise that he leads the country in receiving yards and touchdowns entering this week’s matchup with Washington State. “You see him with ball in space, obviously taking the top off a number of times,” Washington State coach Kirby Moore said. “I think it’s about playing team defense. Obviously communication is going to be really important, where he’s at.” The Cougars (1-5, 0-2 Pac-12) have the No. 2 defense in the Pac-12 thus far and are having that success by keeping the top on their pass coverage. WSU has allowed 11 passes of 30-plus yards, which is tied for 129th nationally and nearly 10% of the passes it has allowed. However, opponents are not breaking through that mark often, with just four passes over 40 yards and none for more than 50, one of 30 teams yet to allow such a play this season. “We don’t want to let the verticals up,” Washington State safety Jaylen Smith said. “We take pride in (not) letting deep balls go. We always look to play top down and take away the deep routes first.” WSU defensive coordinator Trent Bray will be tasked with doing what nobody has been able to do yet this season: contain Legree. OSU offensive coordinator Mitch Dahlen has been creative in moving Legree around to prevent defenses from taking him away. Last week against San Diego State that included moving Legree into the backfield for a variety of plays. “People are going to try and hit him at the line of scrimmage,” Dahlen said. “They’re going to try and two-hand jam. If they’re going to try and two-hand jam, it’s like OK, how can I move this guy enough where you can’t do that? You put him in the backfield, unless you want to jump offsides and do it, you can’t do it that way. “That’s what we do a good job of as a staff, is moving him around where you can’t just put a safety over the top of him because if he’s in the backfield, what are you going to do there?” Even if the Cougars manage to limit Legree, the Beavers have shown they are more than capable of going elsewhere, with an outrageous 14 players catching passes last week. Aeryn Hampton (20 receptions for 245 yards) and tight ends Eric Olsen and DeCorion Temple each have at least 20 catches and Aaron Butler has four grabs for at least 20 yards. item.title: Klopp's agent reveals he called Uli Hoeneß following criticism of his Germany role
item.description: Klopp's agent reveals he called Uli Hoeneß following criticism of his Germany role When Jürgen Klopp was appointed Germany's national team coach following the World Cup, he brought his agent, Marc Kosicke, on board in an advisory role. The decision initially drew criticism from Bayern Munich honorary president Uli Hoeneß, who told RTL/Sky: “He (Kosicke) has a players’ agency, and he is its managing director. He also owns shares in it. I consider that a problem. The whole thing seems like a ‘friendly takeover’ to me. Klopp and co. have taken over the DFB, and I think that is wrong.” Kosicke has now addressed the criticism during an appearance on FFH, revealing that he personally called Hoeneß to discuss the matter. "I called him and left him a voicemail. Then he called me back, and I told him: 'If you have a question, you don't need to ask it publicly. You have my number. Call me and I'll answer all your questions.' Then we managed to clear things up relatively quickly,” Kosicke revealed. The 55-year-old also explained that Klopp had insisted on having him involved in the project. “Jürgen came into a negotiation with me and said: 'Let me make one thing clear: I'm not doing any of this without Marc.' A few people initially nearly fell off their chairs and said: 'Well, what is he supposed to do then? We've already got everything covered,'" Kosicke recalled. "Then Jürgen said: 'You'll figure it out.' They then looked for a title for me, and everything had to be approved by the supervisory boards and presidents. Then Jürgen said: 'Wouldn't it be easier if he became my assistant coach?' They said: 'Yes, that can be done,' and that's how I became an assistant coach," he continued. Kosicke's responsibilities within the coaching staff include strategy, development and innovation.

item.title: Cade Cunningham Makes NBA History With 52-Point Masterpiece
item.description: Detroit Pistons superstar Cade Cunningham delivered a performance for the ages Thursday night, scoring a career-high 52 points to lead Detroit to a thrilling 144-140 double-overtime victory over the Washington Wizards. But it wasn’t just the scoring that made Cunningham’s performance historic. According to NBA.com , Cunningham became the first player in league history to record at least 50 points, 10 assists, and ZERO turnovers in a single game since the NBA began tracking turnovers during the 1977-78 season. That’s right, nobody had ever accomplished that combination in nearly five decades of recorded NBA history. Cunningham finished with 52 points, 11 assists, five rebounds, one steal, and one block while shooting an impressive 16-of-25 from the field. He also knocked down 17 of his 18 free-throw attempts, making this one of the most efficient high-scoring performances in Pistons history. Cunningham then opened the second overtime with a three-pointer before delivering a crucial baseline jumper in the final minute to help seal the victory. item.description: The Boston Celtics have traded for, signed, and drafted players from nearly every U.S. state and countries across the globe.
